RTB - Spoke with Casey and her team. The IPT Lead that the project engineers will be communicating with is Jarrod Hargis (He is over all of the vendors). They need Project Engineers in 4 location over 4 different Vendors. 

Aerohead - Los Alamitos, CA - They Build the core stage of the Feed Lines. Need someone with Structural Feed lines and NDT Experience. Experience in Building Hardware. General Dynamics - Lincoln NB - They do the COPV's (Composite Overwrap Pressure Vessels) of the upper stage and core stage of the rocket. COPV's are a metallic tank wrapped in composite fibers. Pacific Scientific (Pac SCi) - Chandler, AZ - Building the Core Stage and EUS (Exploration Upper Stage) of the Safe and Arm mechanism. This is a device that arms the rocket if it is over land so it can explode before it hits land. It's a component that takes the aircraft from a safe position to an Armed position. Need Someone with Pyrotechnical system Background or Ordinance Position background. Someone with Electromechanical device experience. 

She also connect me with Anthony Hankinson (Program Quality Manager) and Alyssa Helwig (Senior Manager, Space Launch System Production Engineering) for there Michoud Assembly Facility. They need people over there because of the recent attrition they have gone through. column2: • Effect the Government shutdown is having on the contract. The following areas are being affected by the shutdown:

column3: • Start Dates for new hires. The security team on the government side has taken a hit as many of the team are not working due to the shutdown. Mentioned only a handful of the government security team is working. This has caused delays in onboarding due to not being able to brief contractors for their SCI.

This is causing delays in onboarding as well since GDIT will not bring a new hire onto a team that is running low on funding. This also could affect current contractors if the government shutdown is not over soon. Said some of the CUP’s might have contractors work at-risk or even stop work completely.

• Pause on the 90 new spots that were slated to be added to the contract in Q4. Mentioned that if the government shutdown continues, the new MOD with the 90 spots will more than likely be pushed to March 2026.

column2: • Jon Miner has been relieved from his role as the NCR lead and Pam McComas will be taking over duties for the time being. GDIT is actively working to find a replacement but did not provide a timeline of when that will be. Pam has a few candidates in mind and mentioned if the candidates she has in mind fall through, they might allow subs to help with the sourcing.

Mentioned only a handful of the government security team is working. This has caused delays in onboarding due to not being able to brief contractors for their SCI.

<li>There could be issues with funding for certain CUP’s as the funding for this contract is incremental and there are a few CUP’s whose funding runs out in mid-November. This is causing delays in onboarding as well since GDIT will not bring a new hire onto a team that is running low on funding. This also could affect current contractors if the government shutdown is not over soon. Said some of the CUP’s might have contractors work at-risk or even stop work completely.

<li>Pause on the 90 new spots that were slated to be added to the contract in Q4. Mentioned that if the government shutdown continues, the new MOD with the 90 spots will more than likely be pushed to March 2026.

NotesActivityReport_Main,Atlanta,Matt Capelluto,10/2/2025,Contact,Appointment,Melodey Lawson,New Lead,"Leidos, NASA, NEST: Met with Melodey Lawson on Monday, she’s the Manager for Leidos’ NEST program overseeing all Service Delivery Operations for the contract. She’s in Covington, Louisiana working remote, but her main onsite location is Michoud Assembly Facility (MAF) in New Orleans. She let me know that her teams combined are a total of 190 people, and all of which are in positions focused on delivery of services to over 60,000 NASA personnel. These teams are made up of end-user support specialists, hardware specialists (pc technicians), M365 specialists, logistics, incident response, (mostly lower-level positions). End-user support and help desk personnel work remote, while the rest are all onsite. She let me know that most of the engineers and senior leadership are within the Enterprise Operations division. The employees and contractors under her division are more widely distributed across the different NASA locations, which include Orlando, Huntsville, Houston, New Orleans, Stennis, and White Sands facility in New Mexico. She said her most utilized sub is a small named EMCO technologies, asked why they use them and she said they have been partners for a while, and they bring Microsoft and nasa expertise.
